subject: Post-demo recap — deployment venue options & migration constraints
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Gupta <anita@healthlytogether.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — deployment venue options & migration constraints

Hi Anita — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and a couple of targeted questions to help us size the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private). I know you want a short checklist we can circulate to procurement.

Recap / our understanding:
- Primary concern: PHI data flows from your intake pipeline; compliance & VPC isolation are must-haves.
- Current state: a self-hosted GPU cluster (onprem-gpu-01) running an in-house LLM serving stack; some traffic is already routed through VeloxAI endpoints for inference.
- Target SLA: 99.9% regional uptime, p95 latency < 200ms for single-request generation on short prompts.
- Expected steady-state: ~350 QPS token-generation requests during peak; bursts to 1.2k QPS for 30–60 minutes.

Questions we need answered to recommend the deployment venue: 
1) Data residency: do all inference requests need to remain in your VPC / on-prem? Or is a managed VPC peering arrangement acceptable for the POC?
2) Migration tolerance for model artifacts: do you require a full binary lift-and-shift of your current quantized checkpoints, or are you open to running an equivalent Redwood-verified quantized variant?
3) KV/prefix cache portability: you mentioned 24 hours of session cache retention — is migrating the existing KV cache required or can we start fresh and warm the cache during the POC?
4) Procurement window & decision owner: who will sign the PoC SOW? Can procurement respond within 10 business days?

Recommended next steps (proposed):
- Short technical POC (2 weeks) using Dedicated capacity with VPC peering to validate latency and traffic patterns, plus a follow-on on-prem evaluation if data residency requires it.
- Karthik to scope Resource/Capacity estimate.
- Mina to prepare a checklist for SOC2/PHI artifacts we will share for procurement.

Attachments: scope doc + deploy-options comparison + high-level dataflow (see attached stubs).

If you can answer the 4 questions above, we’ll send a tailored PoC SOW and a recommended capacity profile. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up next week.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: healthy_together_poc_scope_v1.pdf (7KB stub), redwood_deploy_options_comparison.xlsx (12KB stub), data_flow_diagram.png (45KB stub)

From: Anita Gupta <anita@healthlytogether.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthlytogether.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@healthlytogether.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment venue options & migration constraints

Hi Markus — great demo, thanks. Answers inline below.

1) Data residency: For PHI we need all inference traffic and logs to remain within our VPC or on-prem. For the POC we are open to a managed VPC peering arrangement (if peering + strict IAM/KMS controls are in place).

2) Model artifacts: We currently run a custom quantized variant (Q4B) that has a few tokenization differences. Ideally we’d like bit-for-bit parity for the critical intents before cutting over, but we are open to Redwood running a verified equivalent if you can demonstrate parity on our eval set. We’ll provide a small evaluation harness.

3) KV/prefix cache: We prefer to migrate session state where possible, but we understand moving KV snapshots is non-trivial. For the POC, warming the cache during traffic replay is acceptable; long-term we’ll want an approach to export/import the cache (or a sync mechanism).

4) Procurement: I’m the product owner; Raj will own procurement sign-off. Target window: 3 weeks for PoC approval if all artifacts are provided quickly.

Additional constraints:
- Peak QPS: expected 1.2k (burst). Steady 350 QPS.
- Latency targets: p95 <200ms on our short prompts; 400–600ms acceptable for longer context runs.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration required for key management; SOC2 Type II evidence preferred.

Next step: please send a POC SOW that reflects a Dedicated-first approach with VPC peering and a clear escalation path to Private/on-prem packaging if the residency requirement forces a full on-prem deployment.

—Anita
Anita Gupta
Sr. Product Manager, HealthyTogether
anita@healthlytogether.com

Attachment: procurement_contact_card.vcf (stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap — deployment venue options & migration constraints

Karthik / Mina — forwarding Anita’s replies. Quick internal plan and asks so we can produce the PoC SOW by EOD Monday.

Technical assumptions I want validated:
- POC mode: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) + managed VPC peering to HealthyTogether VPC. This lets us validate latency & burst handling without shipping on-prem code immediately. If residency fails at procurement, we escalate to full Private on-prem (packaged agent).
- Model compatibility: we need to run their evaluation harness against our verified quantized variant. Karthik: can we schedule 2hrs with Applied ML to confirm tokenization parity and a runbook for model artifact conversion?
- KV export/import: Mina — produce a short brief (1 page) of options: snapshot export, streaming sync, or rebuild/warm via replay. Include rough engineering effort (S, M, L).
- Capacity: ballpark Dedicated capacity to hit 1.5k peak QPS with room for headroom — provide instance mix + estimated monthly committed GPU-hours. We want a guesstimate to include in the SOW.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: scope capacity + technical POC runbook (ETA: Mon 2028-03-13 EOD).
- Mina: security artifacts checklist & KV migration brief (ETA: Mon 2028-03-13 noon).
- Markus: draft SOW and commercial anchor (PoC pricing + optional Private packaging) — aim to send to Anita on Mon afternoon.

We should propose a 30-min follow-up Tue/Thu next week. I’ll include a timeslot sheet in the SOW email.

—Markus
